doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: Thelonious Monk's non-interview at the Royal Arms
summary: Description of the Royal Arms and the attempt to interview Monk, who mimed swimming in bed; talk of sons following fathers, including Ravi Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: big Cleaners, it was a jazz night club, they called it the Royal Arms and they created a shield, you know with two blades crossing, R on one side and at the bottom was A. And there was a stage that you walked up five steps to, and it was like a semi-circle. It had a semi-circle bar and there was a space between the edge of that stage and where the three cash registers were. And you could actually fall off that stage if you got too far into the stage. And you walked up those five steps to get on the stage. So Jimmy said, “Charlie, Charlie, I talked to Nellie (the wife of Monk) and I told them I’ve got this white kid who really knows a lot about jazz, and could he get an interview?” And she says, “Well you know I think so, maybe Friday night. Tell him to come before the 9:30 show.” So I came at 8:00. And so he was there. I said he’s got to be there. And he goes “Oh don’t worry I’ll take you up and I’ll introduce you to Nellie.” So he knocks on the door, “Nellie, this is Chuck,” you know, our basketball pal and a jazz guy. So is Monk ready to do a brief interview with Chuck?” So I had a whole bunch of questions. And she goes, “Well I’m not so sure right now.” So she goes to ask Monk. “Thelonious, the young man is here.” Dadadada. He’s on the bed. And so she opens the door and she goes, “You know, Chuck, I don’t think he’s going to do an interview tonight.” She opened the door so I could see, he is doing a simulated backstroke as if he’s swimming. Like this. And he’s not stopping. I guess that was a message that he was not going to do an interview. So Jimmy looks at me and I go, “we tried. It’s okay.” I always have this story.
Yes. It makes for a good story. And today’s his birthday.
Well I’m so glad that his son picked up the mantle after trying the rhythm & blues world for a couple of years. It’s just like Natalie Cole. You want to do what your father did.
Yeah. Speaking of that, Ravi Coltrane came to Hamilton once. And he looked so much like his father. And I was sitting next to him and it was a very weird feeling.
